commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[grafana] Ask finelog which namespaces it holds (#9186)

Bumps marin-finelog so the producers route can ask the deployment which
namespaces it holds, instead of naming each one and reading the error
when it is absent.

- The bridge pins a development release, the first to carry
`list_namespaces`. No stable release has it, and the lock resolved the
June stable wheel.
- That lock also moves marin-rigging and adds pydantic, because the
newer finelog needs the newer rigging. Bumping finelog alone leaves a
lock whose connection helper fails to import.
- The route queries only the RL namespaces the deployment holds, so a
statement never names an absent table.

Checked against the hub with the new client: the route answers 200 with
the producer rows of last night's nightly run, and the listing takes
about 0.1 s.

Follows #9123, where the route dropped an absent namespace by matching
DataFusion's missing-table message.

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
Upgrade FA4 to fix H100 sparse backward race (#8741)

Upgrade FA4 from beta16 to beta28 to fix a race in H100 block-sparse
backward that can corrupt gradients or produce NaNs. The [upstream
fix](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2756) landed in
beta26; beta27 added compatibility with CUTLASS 4.6.2. The lockfile
selects beta28.

Update the launchers for the new API. Explicit padded scratch offsets
preserve beta16's effective behavior. Quack 0.6.4 and CUTLASS 4.6.2 stay
unchanged; apache-tvm-ffi moves from 0.1.10 to 0.1.14.

On 64 GB200s, beta16 and beta28 produced identical logged losses across
nine frozen batches, repeated three times each. Sampled gradient
differences between versions were 1.75–4.76% in relative L2, within the
observed 1.54–5.17% range between repeats of the same version. All
measurements were finite. Gradient comparisons sample up to 4096
coordinates per parameter leaf.
[Analysis](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fheld%2Ffa4-8741-frozen-analysis-20260915).

The training comparison repeated [Matt's one-rack
test](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8959#issuecomment-5606628341):
100 training updates from checkpoint 80912, with the same hero model,
optimizer, batch size 1024, and sequence length 4096. Both arms used 64
GB200s at Production priority:
[control](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fheld%2Ffa4-8741-hero-control-20260915-production-coord)
at `a428f1d25d53` and
[treatment](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fheld%2Ffa4-8741-hero-treatment-20260915-production-coord)
at `cbbb9f45caa2`. Both arms completed all 100 updates with zero task
failures or nonfinite logged values. Mean loss was 1.273384 for control
and 1.273395 for beta28 (mean signed difference +0.0000111; maximum
absolute per-step loss difference 0.00110). Median step time after the
first 10 updates was 16.03s for control and 15.90s for beta28.

Three earlier H100 runs resumed with finite losses, but they predate the
rebase. The rebased branch still needs H100 validation; the GB200
comparison does not test the H100 kernel or full-scale hero stability.
See [Echo 269](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/269) for the incident history.

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
Retain hero completion history across sampling versions (#9211)

Keep completed hero samples in the latest report when the sampling
specification changes. Update the report only after new results with
completion text arrive. A new specification with no completions leaves
the report unchanged.

Read historical result formats and mark missing probabilities as
unavailable. The public result files retain their original JSON. Skip
malformed result files, and display each comparison panel even if the
other result fails to load. Scheduling still uses the current sampling
specification.

All 22 focused tests passed. Browser checks passed with historical
formats, missing scores, and a failed result request.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[finestore] Read archives whose format marker expired (#9202)

- `ReadView` no longer refuses a `HEAD` without `_archive.json`. Version
1 archives have no `HEAD`, and `read_snapshot` checks the format version
that `HEAD` carries, so the marker adds nothing for a populated archive.
The next writer open recreates it, as before.
- `PersistentKvCache.load` and the local `store` path catch `Exception`,
matching the remote write queue. The cache is best-effort, so an
unreadable, corrupt, or unsupported archive degrades to a recompile.

The GPU canary crashed on 2026-09-16 (#9194). The cutlass kernel cache
at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/cutlass-kernels` lost its
write-once marker to the 30-day lifecycle rule, while `HEAD`, which
every commit rewrites, remained. The bucket reports `X-Amz-Expiration`
as last-modified plus 30 days, so every write-once object expires on its
own clock. Nothing recreated the marker because the crash came before
any store, and only a writer open recreates it.

Schema objects expire the same way. A missing one is already an
`OSError` miss, and the writer open behind the next store recreates it.
Readers recompile at most once per 30 days of writer inactivity. The
`marin-us-east-02a` schema object is already gone, so the first run with
this change recompiles once and heals it. An earlier revision of this PR
rewrote the marker and schema objects from the commit path to avoid that
one recompile. It needed interval state, a local-versus-remote gate, and
conflict handling, so this revision removes it.

Operational steps beyond merging:

- [x] Recreate the marker to unblock the GPU canary before the fix
ships. Done 2026-09-16 18:58 UTC with `rclone rcat --s3-no-check-bucket
marin-cw:marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/cutlass-kernels/_archive.json`;
the object now expires 2026-10-17. Without `--s3-no-check-bucket`,
rclone tries `CreateBucket` and fails with `InvalidRegion`.
- [ ] Run the CoreWeave canary (`marin-canary-ferry-coreweave.yaml`,
scheduled at 10:00 UTC, or `workflow_dispatch`) from a checkout that
contains this change. `iris cluster start --fresh` builds the task image
from that checkout. Check that the run completes step 1. Expect one full
recompile on that run and hits on the next.
- [ ] Land a fix for #9206 before 2026-09-29. On that date a
never-compacted shard in the hero cluster's `cutlass-kernels` archive
expires and every process there recompiles every kernel on every start.
The `marin-us-east-02a` archive follows on 2026-10-08. Deleting the
archive root is the only recovery today.
- [ ] The fused cross-entropy autotune cache uses the same path. Its
`gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=30d/levanter_kernel_autotune/fused_cross_entropy_loss/block_sizes_v2`
archive dates from 2026-08-25 with no commit since, so its marker and
`HEAD` expire together on 2026-09-24. If an unfixed TPU job commits
there before then, `HEAD` outlives the marker and unfixed readers crash.
A fixed writer recreates it, or recreate it with `gcloud storage cp`.

Fixes #9194

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Fix Gemma FLOP undercount and a quadratic dashboard worker scan (#9195)

`GemmaConfig.flops_per_token` passed `glu=False` to
`lm_flops_per_token`, counting the
MLP as two projections. Gemma decoder layers build `LlamaMlp`, which
runs `gate_proj`,
`up_proj`, and `down_proj`, so the MLP term was two thirds of its true
value and
reported throughput and MFU for Gemma, Gemma2, and Gemma3 runs has been
low since the
FLOP calculations landed. Gemma was the last `glu=False` outlier among
the gated-MLP
models; gpt2 and apertus have ungated MLPs and are already correct.

`CoordinatorDashboard.workers` merged counters one worker at a time, and
each merge
rescanned all of `_worker_counters` to filter for that worker. The map
is keyed by
`(worker_id, execution_id)`, so listing workers was quadratic in pool
size while
holding the coordinator lock that also serves `pull_task`,
`report_result`, and
`heartbeat`. Grouping entries by worker in a single pass leaves merge
order, and
therefore results, unchanged.

The rest is dead code. `WorkerView.attributes` in the Iris controller
test helpers was
always `{}` because `WORKER_DETAIL_COLS` selects no such column;
`make_gcp_provider`
never read the `ScaleGroupConfig` its call sites passed, which implied
the fake
provider was configured from the scale group; and the markdown converter
carried an
unused regex plus two commented-out blocks from 2024. The note
explaining why the
layout-table paragraph check stays off is kept as prose.

---------

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[tasktrove] Harden math answer grading (#9163)

Treat empty or unterminated final boxed answers as incorrect.
Previously,
permissive math parsing could recover an earlier boxed answer from
output that
ended with a malformed `\boxed{` and award full credit.

Reject numeric specs with nonfinite or negative tolerances and with
nonfinite
effective tolerances. Generate the negative verification probe beyond
the
effective tolerance, using the same contract validation as the grader.
Add
tuple comparison and math and numeric spec serialization coverage.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Upload XLA dumps to temporary storage (#9155)

Upload XLA compiler dumps to 30-day lifecycle storage when
`trainer.xla_dump_upload.enabled` is set. Each host sends its initial
dump tree,
then new or modified files after complete hook passes, to
`xla-dumps/<run-id>/process-<n>`.

`XLA_FLAGS=--xla_dump_to=...` remains the opt-in capture control and
must be
set before Python starts. The dumps bypass W&B artifacts; `ttl_days`
controls
their storage lifetime.

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
Score hero references with stable tokenization and EOS (#9199)

Encode each prompt and reference together. Require the combined encoding
to start with the exact tokens from the prompt alone. For two Python
prompts and three list prompts, move the initial reference newline to
the end of the prompt. This gives generation and reference scoring the
same prompt tokens with normal tokenization.

Score a final end-of-sequence (EOS) token after each reference,
including its log probability and the top five tokens at that position.
Show EOS and colored newline markers in the report. Default to the
latest checkpoint on the right and the previous checkpoint on the left,
while preserving explicit URL selections.

The sampler release and prompt changes produce new request IDs, so
reports select results from the updated configuration. Existing results
require new sampling runs to get the corrected scores.

All 46 prompt/reference pairs preserve their prompt tokens and decode
exactly with the pinned tokenizer. All 22 focused tests, type checks,
lint, and browser checks pass.

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
Generate three hero completions per prompt on 32 GPUs (#9189)

Generate three completions per prompt and checkpoint with distinct,
repeatable seeds. Save generated-token log probabilities and the five
most likely alternatives for each sample. Compute expected-answer
probabilities once per prompt and checkpoint. Display all three samples
in the [hero checkpoint
report](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/hero-completions/latest/index.html).

Filter saved requests by the current prompt bank and generation settings
before schema validation. Exclude historical requests from retries and
their results from publication, so older schemas cannot block the
publisher. The new sampler release identifier creates fresh requests for
retained checkpoints. The current report will be empty until results
from this release arrive.

Reduce each checkpoint job from 64 to 32 GB200 GPUs across eight nodes,
with a batch size of 32 per job. This permits two jobs within a 64-GPU
budget when node resources are available. GPU memory use and throughput
still need a live run.

The 22 focused tests, lint, scoped type checks, and local browser checks
passed. An abstract-mesh check confirmed that model tensor dimensions
support 32-GPU sharding.

Part of #8827.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[grafana] Fix the RL run view and list recent runs on Home (#9123)

Makes the RL view usable on a run that has finished, and reachable
without knowing its address.

- The producers panel reads from a new bridge route, which queries each
RL namespace separately and skips any the deployment does not have.
- The view is renamed "RL Post-training", opens on 24 hours, and selects
the most recent run.
- Legends show the series without its column name, generated tokens move
to a second axis, and four titles name the runs they apply to.
- Home shows a "Recent RL runs" table, and each row opens the view on
that run.
- A launch request whose runtime profile disagrees with its effective
`trainer.strategy`, after overrides, is rejected.

Checked against a nightly run: 16 panels, 0 errors, 14 with data. The
uid is unchanged, so old links still work.
